candidates.attacker_control: The rest-of-path of an HTTP request to any URL bound to DirectoryBrowserSupport: workspace browsing (AbstractProject.doWs), artifact browsing (Run.doArtifact), file-parameter browsing (FileParameterValue.doDynamic) and /userContent. An authenticated user with the corresponding read permission (Item.WORKSPACE / Run.ARTIFACTS when enabled / equivalent) controls the path segment(s), including encoded or backslash variants that can survive container normalization.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: (1) `getPath()` normally returns a path beginning with '/' (getRestOfPath semantics are relied on elsewhere, e.g. CLIAction line 105 and Jenkins.doJnlpJars line 4400), which reduces the bypass to the exact '/..' form and often triggers the redirect branch at lines 309-315 instead of a listing. (2) The code contains a separate absolute-path guard (SECURITY-2481, lines 266-271) and symlink/tmp-dir guards (lines 275-278) that prevent some alternative escapes. (3) I could not diff this line against the upstream 2.504 source or run code/tests (no tests or .git are in scope), so it is possible this exact guard is upstream and the residual behavior is considered acceptable/limited. (4) Alternative candidates were checked and considered weaker/unrelated (doLoginEntry and doIconSize open redirects appear to be long-standing upstream legacy code; the unescaped `icon` interpolation in src/main/js search/command-palette rendering needs plugin-controlled icon data and core-only installs never emit a user-controlled image icon; keepReadabilityOnlyOnDescendants is uncalled but several other private helpers (zip/sendZipUsingMap/...) are also dead legacy code, so this is not conclusive evidence of a removed security call).
candidates.impact: Directory/file disclosure outside the intended workspace/artifact/userContent root, at minimum the parent directory listing or ZIP archive of the level above the configured root, and potentially arbitrary readable-path access if a rest-of-path without the leading '/' is ever produced (FilePath.resolvePathIfRelative/normalize will then resolve a leading '../'). Exposes build/job configuration, logs, and other users' workspace files that the requesting permission was not meant to grant.
candidates.prerequisites: A user able to reach a DirectoryBrowserSupport-backed endpoint, and a request path in which a '..' segment is not surrounded by '/' on both sides (at minimum the exact "/.." path, or a leading '..' when the container/Stapler supplies a rest-of-path without the leading '/'). Container-dependent path normalization is needed for '..' to survive routing; default ALLOW_SYMLINK_ESCAPE=false does not prevent '..'-based escaping because only symlinks are checked.
candidates.root_cause: serveFile() validates the request rest-of-path with `path.replace('\\', '/').contains("/../")`. That guard only blocks '..' when it is an interior segment surrounded by '/' (and only after backslash normalization). A path whose '..' is the first segment (e.g. "/..", or "../..." if getRestOfPath() ever lacks the leading '/') or the final segment ("/..", "/foo/..") passes the guard. The remaining path is tokenized into `_base`/`_rest` and passed to `root.child(base)`; FilePath construction then calls normalize(resolvePathIfRelative(base, rel)), which resolves '..' segments and can move the VirtualFile root outside the intended base directory. The file contains an explicit absolute-path rejection (SECURITY-2481) but no equivalent '..' normalization/descendant check, so the validation is the only barrier.
candidates.title: DirectoryBrowserSupport dot-dot validation is incomplete before resolving the browse root via root.child(base)
candidates.trace: HTTP request -> Stapler dispatches to DirectoryBrowserSupport.generateResponse (line 163) -> serveFile (line 205) -> getPath(req) returns req.getRestOfPath() (lines 502-507) -> guard at line 216 accepts the path because '..' is not preceded and followed by '/' (or is the whole remaining segment) -> tokenizer builds `_base` (lines 224-256) -> `base = _base.toString()` -> `root.child(base)` (line 272) -> VirtualFile.child -> FilePathVF.child -> new FilePath(f, name) -> normalize(resolvePathIfRelative(...)) (FilePath.java lines 278-296) resolves '..' and yields a file/dir outside the configured browse root -> outside file is listed/zipped/served (directory index, *plain*/ *zip* branches, or single-file serving at lines 279-428).
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. I did not execute Jenkins, send requests, or inspect container/Stapler normalization behavior; whether a '..' token can actually reach serveFile depends on the servlet container and URL encoding used. I also could not verify whether the current guard differs from upstream 2.504, so this may be an upstream design limitation rather than an introduced defect.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

coverage_summary: Coverage: 9,959 visible files under the assigned root (main sources/resources for core, cli and war modules; tests, Jelly/HTML templates and invisible/over-limit files are filtered out by the harness; no .git). I read or searched the security-critical areas: hudson/security (CSRF filter, crumb issuer, security realm, remember-me), jenkins/security (api tokens, class filter, resource domain, ExtendedRead redaction, BasicHeader auth), DirectoryBrowserSupport and its VirtualFile/FilePath support code, Run/AbstractItem/View/ListView/ItemGroupMixIn/User/Computer permission checks, Jenkins.java root actions, CLI command framework, console notes and annotated large text, JSON signature validator, XMLUtils XXE protection, FilePath.unzip zip-slip guard, Secret/ApiTokenStore crypto paths, and the 2025-era additions (jenkins/cli/listeners, jenkins/management/AdministrativeMonitorsApi, jenkins/console, jenkins/model/details, search UI JS). I did not exhaustively read all ~5,000 Java files; my selection prioritized attacker-reachable request handlers, path/file sinks, auth checks, deserialization and rendering paths.
limitations: No tests, no .git history, and no upstream/patched reference in scope, so I could not confirm which code differs from the upstream 2.504 release or identify the intended ground-truth change.

No code execution, compilation, static analysis, or HTTP requests were performed; all conclusions are source-reading only and the container/Stapler normalization behavior that governs exploitability of the DirectoryBrowserSupport path check is unverified.
Jelly/view templates and other filtered file types were not visible, so any issue whose sink is in a view template could not be assessed.
Large files (e.g. Jenkins.java, Run.java, UpdateCenter.java) were reviewed by targeted searches rather than fully read, so an introduced defect in an unread region cannot be ruled out.

The submitted candidate is a lead with low confidence, not a confirmed vulnerability; exploitability depends on container path handling and on the request path starting or ending with a bare '..' segment.

rejected_leads.lead: Jenkins.doLoginEntry uses from.startsWith("/") && !from.equals("/loginError") to decide the post-login redirect, so `from=//attacker.example` is accepted (open redirect).
rejected_leads.reason: Insufficient validation is real, but this is long-standing legacy code only used by LegacySecurityRealm (testing/dev realm); modern path uses AuthenticationSuccessHandler with Util.isSafeToRedirectTo. Not the strongest distinct issue and likely intentional upstream legacy behavior.

rejected_leads.lead: Jenkins.doIconSize redirects to the raw Referer header (lines 4947-4958).
rejected_leads.reason: Classic open-redirect pattern but appears to be long-standing upstream behavior, no evidence in this snapshot of it being the introduced/patched issue.

rejected_leads.lead: src/main/js/components/command-palette/models.js and src/main/js/components/search-bar/index.js interpolate the search-suggestion `icon` (and in search-bar also `url`) into HTML without escaping, while escaping `label` with xmlEscape.
rejected_leads.reason: Server-side Search.Item.icon is core-generated SVG (symbol type, intentionally HTML) or a UserAvatarResolver URL; core implements no avatar resolver, so attacker-controlled icon data requires a plugin. Label and (in the command palette) URL are escaped. Unconfirmed as the target issue.

rejected_leads.lead: DirectoryBrowserSupport.keepReadabilityOnlyOnDescendants plus the private zip/sendZipUsingMap/sendZipUsingListOfNames/collectRecursivelyAllLegalChildren helpers are never called from any visible source file, which could indicate a removed filtering call for glob/child listings.
rejected_leads.reason: Dead private legacy code exists as a cluster in this class (the zip helper cluster is likewise unreferenced), and the same file's VirtualFile.list/Descriptor paths already drop symlinks/tmp dirs via OptionalDiscardingFileFilter, so this is not conclusive evidence of a removed security control.

rejected_leads.lead: Search.getSuggestionsImpl parses the `max` request parameter with Integer.parseInt without bounds checking, and doSuggest exposes icon/name/group metadata.
rejected_leads.reason: Only a possible 500/DOS-by-exception on a malformed parameter; Search.getTarget requires Jenkins.READ and result sets are permission-filtered through the search index. No clear security impact.

rejected_leads.lead: CLI.js/CLICommand allow custom CLIListener extensions to observe command args/auth (new 2025 code).
rejected_leads.reason: Listener invocation is inside CLICommand.main with the caller's authentication; the default listener logs only argument counts. Extension classes are trusted code; no concrete privilege boundary crossed.

summary: Reviewed the Jenkins core 2.504-SNAPSHOT source snapshot (main sources/resources only; tests and git history are absent). I focused on attacker-controlled HTTP/CLI input reaching validation, path handling, authentication/authorization checks, deserialization, page/response rendering, and the newest 2025 code (CLI listeners, administrative-monitor API, search UI, workspace/artifact browsing). I verified a large set of known security controls are present and correct (CLI @-syntax disabled via ALLOW_AT_SYNTAX, console-note MAC verification, XStream2/JEP-200 filters, artifact/wipeout/script/restart permission checks, CSRF filter canonicalization, safe-redirect helper, zip-slip guard in FilePath.unzip, API-token constant-time compare, ExtendedRead redaction). The single strongest source-level anomaly I found is in DirectoryBrowserSupport: the directory-browser path validation only rejects the literal substring "/../" after backslash normalization, so ".." as a complete leading/final path segment is not rejected before the value is passed to root.child(base) and resolved by FilePath normalization. Because this code is the common sink for workspace browsing, artifact browsing, file-parameter browsing and userContent browsing, a crafted rest-of-path can make the browse root resolve outside the intended base (or at minimum one level above it). Uncertainty is high: I could not diff against upstream, the request path normally starts with '/', and container/Stapler normalization plus the directory-redirect branch constrain which crafted paths actually reach the sink, so impact is limited/conditional rather than proven. I therefore submit one low/medium-confidence candidate and no additional candidates.
